results.title: Thermal Boundary Conditions → Term
results.content: The fundamental **definition** of thermal boundary conditions establishes these parameters; they specify the temperature or heat flux at the surfaces of a system undergoing thermal analysis. The temperatures on the interior and exterior surfaces, or the rate at which heat passes through them, represent the thermal boundary conditions for analyzing heat transfer through that wall. * **Robin Boundary Condition** → Also termed a convective boundary condition, this type relates the heat flux across the boundary to the temperature difference between the surface and the surrounding fluid or environment, using a convection heat transfer coefficient. > Thermal boundary conditions are the essential constraints that dictate temperature or heat flow at a system’s edges. Whether using water tanks or phase change materials, predicting their charging and discharging rates necessitates precisely defining the thermal boundary conditions at their interfaces with the heat source/sink fluid and the surrounding environment. Moving beyond the foundational understanding, an intermediate perspective on thermal boundary conditions involves appreciating their dynamic nature and their interaction with different modes of heat transfer. This leads to more complex non-linear boundary conditions where the heat flux depends not just on the temperature difference but also on surface properties like emissivity and absorptivity, as well as external factors like solar intensity and ambient radiation temperature. Research published in journals like the ‘International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer’ or ‘Building and Environment’ frequently explores methods for quantifying the impact of fluctuating environmental conditions (wind speed, solar irradiance, ambient temperature) on building energy performance predictions, recognizing these as variable boundary conditions. Furthermore, climate modeling inherently relies on defining thermal boundary conditions at the Earth’s surface (interaction with atmosphere, oceans, land) and radiative boundaries at the top of the atmosphere. Decisions based on models with simplified thermal boundary conditions (e.g., assuming uniform surface properties across a city) can have significant real-world impacts on infrastructure design, resource allocation, and vulnerability assessments to heatwaves. The future academic pursuit in this field involves developing multiscale modeling techniques to bridge the gap between microscale phenomena and macroscale boundary conditions, incorporating machine learning for real-time parameter estimation based on sensor data, and establishing standardized protocols for reporting uncertainty in thermal boundary condition specification in research and industry.

results.title: Exploring The Impact Of Surface Area & Porosity On Material Properties | BSD Instrument
results.content: #### Home / Blog / Exploring the Impact of Surface Area & Porosity on Material Properties. # Exploring the Impact of Surface Area & Porosity on Material Properties. This article systematically examines the definitions of Surface Area & Porosity, explores their synergistic and individual effects on key material properties, and highlights real-world applications where their optimization drives technological innovation. For example, a material with high surface area but low pore connectivity may underperform in applications requiring mass transport, while a highly porous material with large, disconnected pores may lack mechanical stability. For example, in heterogeneous catalysis, a material with high surface area (to maximize active sites) and well-connected mesopores (to facilitate reactant and product transport) will outperform a material with high surface area but disconnected pores (which hinder mass transport). * **Sustainable Fabrication**: Developing low-cost, eco-friendly methods to produce high-surface-area porous materials (e.g., using biomass-derived precursors for activated carbon) to reduce environmental impact. Surface Area & Porosity are indispensable parameters in materials design, shaping a wide range of properties from catalytic activity to mechanical strength.

results.title: Effects of Laser Powder Bed Fusion Process Parameters on Porosity, Liquid Retention, and Thermal and Surface Properties for 316L, CoCrW and Ti6Al4V Alloys - ADS
results.content: ## Effects of Laser Powder Bed Fusion Process Parameters on Porosity, Liquid Retention, and Thermal and Surface Properties for 316L, CoCrW and Ti6Al4V Alloys. The samples were subsequently analyzed for relative porosity, liquid retention, and thermal and surface properties. The production processes conducted at various energy densities yielded porosity levels of approximately 7-32%, 2-20% and 3-16% for 316L, CoCrW and Ti6Al4V materials, respectively, in comparison with the theoretical density. Thermal conductivity values for 316L, CoCrW and Ti6Al4V samples ranged from 15.1 to 12.9, 7.9 to 7.1 and 6.1 to 5.8 W/m.K, respectively. Among the investigated alloys, 316L alloy is determined to have potential for thermal applications (extended surface applications, transpiration cooling, etc.) due to its efficient liquid retention feature, relatively high thermal conductivity and moderate surface roughness. Additionally, relatively easy porosity controlling in 316L alloy LPBF productions and leveraging its ability to fabricate porous structures hold great promise for further advancements in thermal application products.
